question: Should OpenClaw adopt this AI-safety taxonomy, durable audit history, and plugin emission contract as a core product surface, and if so which minimal first slice is owned by core rather than plugins?
rationale: This is not a mechanical bug fix: it establishes new public plugin, Gateway, CLI, persisted-data, exporter, and UI contracts whose long-term scope and privacy posture require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow core foundation
options.body: Define a minimal core event schema and owner boundary first, then split follow-up exporter, persistence, and UI work behind that approved contract.

options.title: Keep it plugin-owned
options.body: Use existing diagnostics and plugin seams for optional governance/exporter functionality, adding only a narrowly justified missing core seam if one is demonstrated.

options.title: Defer the taxonomy
options.body: Do not add the new public contracts until a maintainer-sponsored observability roadmap defines supported events, retention, and operator UX.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core foundation
recommendation.body: Define a minimal core event schema and owner boundary first, then split follow-up exporter, persistence, and UI work behind that approved contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current feature-series author and can provide the concrete proposed boundary, while a repository owner must sponsor the final product decision.
